1.pericope_label: Zedekiah was one and twenty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem
debates: Who wrote this closing chapter and why it stands here
What Zedekiah evil consisted in when no idolatry is recorded
What the prison of Zedekiah was
outliers: Clarke names Ezra as the probable compiler, where the others say only that it was written by someone among the exiles
Ellicott reports a Greek rendering that makes the prison a house of the mill and sets the blinded king to slave work
themes: An appendix added to show a prophecy came true
A king expelled from a presence he had already left
Walls that will not stand without men or God
A son of David arraigned at a heathen bar

12.pericope_label: Now in the fifth month, in the tenth day of the month, which was the nineteenth year of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon
debates: Which day of the fifth month the burning fell on
How long the temple had stood
Whether the opening words about the poor belong to this verse
Why the great brazen furniture was broken instead of carried off
outliers: Ellicott would read all the great houses rather than all the houses of the great men
Henry turns the title chief of the slaughter-men into a general remark, that soldiers are executioners of a sentence God has passed
themes: A month remembered afterwards by fasting
A general who served his king and not the God who used him
Cottages of the poor left standing among ashes
Pillars too vast to move and so broken up

20.pericope_label: The two pillars, one sea, and twelve brasen bulls that were under the bases, which king Solomon had made in the house of the Lord
debates: Whether seven or five men near the king were taken
How the height of the pillar is to be reconciled with the other account
What rank the officers held who were singled out
outliers: Ellicott finds a single principle behind the whole list, that what the exile punished was prominence in the defence of the city
Henry counts the executed at seventy-two and matches the figure to the number of the elders of Israel
themes: Pomegranates counted toward the four winds
A priest whose office could not shield him
Men known for having seen the king face
A land spuing out its people as it once spued out others

28.pericope_label: This is the people whom Nebuchadrezzar carried away captive: in the seventh year three thousand Jews and three and twenty
debates: Why the numbers are so much smaller than the other accounts give
Whether the seventh year is a different year or a different event
What the final deportation five years after the fall was
outliers: Ellicott supposes a word has dropped out of the text and reads the seventeenth year rather than the seventh
Ellicott argues from the size of the return that friends and kindred followed the exiles out to Babylon of their own accord
themes: A narrative parting company with its parallel
Numbers precise enough to imply a register
Prisoners sent off when a siege was lifted
A handful standing for a whole nation

31.pericope_label: And it came to pass in the seven and thirtieth year of the captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah
debates: Why the day of the month differs from the other account
What lifting up the head means
Whether the closing words of the book are genuine
outliers: Ellicott draws from the small textual variations a rule about what belief in the truthfulness of the records does and does not require
Clarke judges the last clause a repetition carried over by mistake and prefers an older rendering that ends the book differently
themes: A prisoner counted out to fifty-five years old
A son undoing what his father had done
Robes changed back into robes again
A census set against a captive list
